verdict: GE Aerospace's orders jumped 49% to $19.0B and revenue rose 16% to $14.1B as LEAP engine deliveries and services boomed; net income was $2.29B after a $124M discontinued-operations loss.

segments.name: Commercial Engines & Services
segments.note: Airliner engines (LEAP, GEnx) and the highly profitable business of servicing them — services revenue and total engine deliveries both grew strongly, with LEAP up 26%.

segments.name: Defense & Propulsion Technologies
segments.note: Military engines and propulsion, including the F414 that powers the F/A-18 — it won a support contract worth up to $2.9B.

segments.name: Insurance & other, net
segments.note: Run-off insurance operations ($833M of revenue) less intersegment eliminations and other items (-$526M) — a legacy business GE is winding down, not growing.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Engine research and development, including the RISE future-engine program.

opex.name: Interest & financial charges
opex.note: Interest and other financial charges, which GE reports inside its total costs and expenses.

otherDetail: Other income of $432M — including $117M of gains on equity securities and $66M of equity-method earnings — less a $124M loss from discontinued operations and $8M of profit attributable to noncontrolling interests: a net $300M in the chart.
footerNote: GE reports one GAAP costs-and-expenses total of $11,745M. The split here follows its 10-Q lines: SG&A ($1,114M), R&D ($458M) and interest and other financial charges ($231M) are the running-cost block; the remaining $9,942M — engine production and services costs, insurance costs and benefit-plan items — is the direct-cost block. GE's own headline 'operating profit' of $2,988M is a non-GAAP measure on adjusted revenue (excluding insurance); the GAAP operating profit implied by this chart is $2,373M, and GAAP pre-tax income from continuing operations was $2,805M.

takeaways.title: Orders are outrunning production
takeaways.text: Orders hit $19.0B — including the largest LEAP agreement ever (1,000+ LEAP-1A engines for IndiGo) — as airlines lock in engines and long-term service deals faster than GE can build them.

takeaways.title: Commercial engines & services boomed
takeaways.text: CES revenue rose 21% to $10.3B with a 27.9% segment profit margin. Services — maintaining the huge installed fleet — are the profit engine, and LEAP deliveries grew 26%.

takeaways.title: Guidance went up again
takeaways.text: Continuing GAAP EPS was $2.32 (+14%) and adjusted EPS $2.25 (+36%); GE raised full-year guidance on year-to-date orders, revenue and deliveries all up over 20%.

oneTimers: A $124M loss from discontinued operations (legacy businesses) sits below the tax line and is included in the chart's other-income line, as explained there.
Other income includes $117M of gains on retained and sold ownership interests and other equity securities.
The run-off insurance business contributed $833M of revenue and $1,043M of costs and expenses inside the GAAP totals; GE's adjusted figures exclude it.
